focus: weighted interpolation, factorization, ramification cleanup, and characteristic-safe propagation

messages.body_markdown: `AE-25`–`AE-28` adopt the component-template route of `E2E-21`–`E2E-23`. The refinement in `AE-26` prunes only point vertices of cleaned degree at most $D$, costing less than $D/p$; component propagation never needs a line-degree lower bound. The generic lift and compression remain drafting because `GENIUS:P8`–`P10` are unaudited and `researcher-0001:P7.1` has enclosing verdict `revise`.
messages.subject: Component-template spine adopted

messages.body_markdown: The mass-only certificate in `AE-12` still suffices. After `AE-29`, retain exactly those cleaned edges whose point endpoint has degree more than $D$; all such point degrees are unchanged because no nonisolated line vertex is subsequently removed. Thus `AE-26` supplies a simple high-direction seed in every component without strengthening the incidence handoff.
messages.subject: Mass-only handoff needs only point pruning

messages.body_markdown: Template compression removes the primary need for irreducible-factor linearization, but it does not remove simple-root cleanup. `AE-27` still starts from $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$ and uses formal implicit uniqueness across every traversed edge. The singular-pencil obstruction `AE-11` rules out replacing this by direction count alone; `AE-19` remains a fallback, not the primary lift.
messages.subject: Compression still requires simple roots

messages.body_markdown: `AE-24` imports the high-popularity-tail decoder from `researcher-0010:[P8].1`. It does not settle `AE-12`: the complementary low-tail case still needs a label-aware decoder-or-rank-reaching argument with retained mass $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ and the strict bound $D\le K_\theta d$.
messages.subject: Residual low-tail obligation unchanged

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence instance
nodes.notes: This fixes the bivariate prime-field regime; no dimension bootstrapping or treatment of $d\le100$ is included.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, and $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$. For every affine line $L$, fix a bijective affine parametrization $\ell_L:\mathbb F_p\to L$ and $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$. Put $$\mathcal I=\{(\ell_L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(\ell_L(t))\},\qquad \mu(E)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)},\qquad \epsilon=\mu(\mathcal I),$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg Q\le d}\frac{|\{x\in\mathbb F_p^2:Q(x)=f(x)\}|}{p^2},$$ where $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ has total degree at most $d$.

nodes.label: Weighted restriction map
nodes.notes: This is the finite-dimensional linear map encoding the supplied line graphs.
nodes.statement_markdown: Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $1,1,d$. For $D\ge d$, put $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}A\le D\},\qquad \rho_L(A)(t)=A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t)),$$ and, for a line family $R$, define $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\longrightarrow\prod_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\longmapsto(\rho_M(A))_{M\in R}.$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching certificate
nodes.notes: The interface uses only retained accepted mass and reached roots; it imposes neither connectivity nor minimum degree.
nodes.statement_markdown: A rank-reaching certificate is $(G,R,D)$ where $G=(X,T,E)$ is a nonempty subgraph of $\mathcal I$, $R\subseteq T$, $D\ge d$, $|R|>D$, and $$\operatorname{rank}(\Phi_{R,D})<\dim V_D.$$ For every $L\in T$, it also satisfies $$\left|\left\{x:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\}\text{ with }(x,M)\in E\right\}\right|>D.$$

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal open incidence obligation. The cited GENIUS step is conjectural and unaudited; the high-popularity result in `AE-24` treats only one subcase. A direct decoder branch is necessary because graph-only reaching families can be expensive on already decodable instances.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, there exist $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge1$ and $0<a_\theta,c_\theta\le1$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta(d/p)^{1-\theta}$$ implies either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta\epsilon,$$ or there is a rank-reaching certificate $(G,R,D)$ satisfying $$\mu(E)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,\qquad D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter gate
nodes.notes: The cited source is unaudited. Elementarily, $D/(\epsilon p)\le(K_\theta/C_\theta)(d/p)^\theta$, so increasing $C_\theta$ supplies all three inequalities.
nodes.statement_markdown: After increasing $C_\theta$ as a function of $a_\theta,K_\theta,\theta$, every certificate alternative in `AE-12` satisfies $$D<p,\qquad \frac{D}{\epsilon p}\le\frac{a_\theta}{100(K_\theta+1)},\qquad \left(\frac Dp\right)^2+\frac{2D}{p}\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{4}.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: Radicalization preserves every selected-line identity because each restriction lies in the domain $\mathbb F_p[t]$. The condition $|R|>D$ excludes a base-only radical, and $D<p$ then gives $A_Z\ne0$. The accepted researcher step is a parameter-specific analogue; the rank-general assembly remains drafting.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the certificate alternative, there exists a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\ne0,
\qquad \rho_M(A)=0\quad\text{for every }M\in R.$$

nodes.label: Reached-root identity extension
nodes.notes: Each reached accepted point is a root of a restriction of degree at most $D$; more than $D$ distinct roots force the identity.
nodes.statement_markdown: For the relation $A$ from `AE-14`, $$\rho_L(A)=0\qquad\text{for every }L\in T.$$

nodes.label: Primitive whole-relation normalization
nodes.notes: Coefficient-content removal is performed before any separability claim. The GENIUS assembly is unaudited; the accepted researcher step supplies the corresponding normalization in the component construction.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Write $$A=HB,$$ where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the gcd of the $Z$-coefficients of $A$, $h=\deg H$, and $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}B$. Then $B$ is squarefree, primitive, and $Z$-dependent, with $$d\le\Delta,
\qquad h+\Delta\le D.$$ If $$T_H=\{L\in T:H(\ell_L(t))=0\text{ in }\mathbb F_p[t]\},$$ then $|T_H|\le h$ and $$B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0\qquad(L\in T\setminus T_H).$$

nodes.label: Characteristic-safe vertical resultant
nodes.notes: Both cited inputs have exact accept audits. Primitivity removes base-only factors, while $\Delta\le D<p<dp$ makes every $Z$-dependent irreducible factor separable. The raw Sylvester resultant is used without division by a leading coefficient; when $r=1$, its second input is constant in $Z$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $$r=\deg_ZB\ge1,
\qquad \gamma=\operatorname{wdeg}(B_Z).$$ Then $$B_Z\ne0,
\qquad \gcd(B,B_Z)=1,
\qquad \gamma\le\Delta-d.$$ The number $b_B$ of labeled affine lines satisfying both $$B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0,
\qquad B_Z(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0$$ is at most $$b_B\le(r-1)\Delta+r\gamma-dr(r-1)\le\frac{\Delta^2}{d}-\Delta.$$

nodes.label: Whole-relation ramification cleanup
nodes.notes: The sharp separability and resultant inputs are accepted through `AE-09`, but this rank-general cleanup package has no standalone accept audit. All content and identically ramified lines are removed before pointwise derivative roots are counted.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Define $$T_{\mathrm{exc}}=T_H\cup\{L\in T\setminus T_H:B_Z(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0\},$$ and $$E_0=\{(x,L)\in E:L
otin T_{\mathrm{exc}},\ B_Z(x,f(x))
e0\}.$$ Then $$|T_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le rac{D^2}{d}-D$$ and $$\mu(E\setminus E_0)\le rac{D^2/d-D}{p(p+1)}+ rac{D-d}{p}\le\left( rac Dpight)^2+ rac Dp.$$ Every $(x,L)\in E_0$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))
e0,$$ and every line incident to $E_0$ satisfies $B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0$.

nodes.label: One-sided high-direction pruning
nodes.notes: This sharpens the cited two-shore peeling arguments. The deletion is simultaneous on the point shore; all edges of every retained point are kept, and nonisolated low-degree lines are not deleted. The exact refinement has no standalone audit.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $$X_1=\{x:\deg_{E_0}(x)>D\},
\qquad E_1=\{(x,L)\in E_0:x\in X_1\},$$ and let $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ contain the nonisolated line vertices. Then $$\mu(E_0\setminus E_1)\le\frac{D}{p+1}<\frac Dp,
\qquad \mu(E_1)\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2}.$$ Every $x\in X_1$ has more than $D$ distinct incident lines in $G_1$ and satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$ Every $L\in T_1$ satisfies $B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0$.

nodes.label: Componentwise formal lift
nodes.notes: At a point seed, formal implicit recursion divides only by the nonzero scalar $B_Z(x,f(x))$. More than $D$ directions kill homogeneous branch terms through degree $D<p$, giving the global identity; one-variable simple-root uniqueness then propagates it through the component. The GENIUS step is unaudited, researcher-0001 has enclosing verdict `revise`, and researcher-0002 proves the packaged component case.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every connected component $\Gamma=(X_\Gamma,T_\Gamma,E_\Gamma)$ of $G_1$, there exists $Q_\Gamma\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))=0$$ and $$Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)
\qquad(x\in X_\Gamma).$$

nodes.label: Template compression and aggregation
nodes.notes: The monic linear polynomials $Z-Q$ are distinct prime divisors of the common relation $B$. Edge mass is grouped by template, and $|E_Q|\le(p+1)|X_Q|$ converts the winning group directly to point agreement. Both cited steps are unaudited.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $$\mathcal Q=\{Q_\Gamma:\Gamma\text{ is a connected component of }G_1\}.$$ For every $Q\in\mathcal Q$, $$Z-Q\mid B,$$ and consequently $$1\le|\mathcal Q|\le\deg_ZB\le\frac{D}{d}\le K_\theta.$$ Some $Q\in\mathcal Q$ satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{\mu(E_1)}{|\mathcal Q|}\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2K_\theta}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional fixed-theta algebraic engine
nodes.notes: The direct alternative of `AE-12` gives the first constant, while `AE-28` gives the second. This theorem remains blocked on `AE-12` and on standalone audits of the generalized downstream assemblies.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, assuming `AE-12`, there exist $C_\theta^*,c_\theta^*>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta^*(d/p)^{1-\theta}$$ implies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta^*\epsilon.$$ One may take $$c_\theta^*=\min\left\{c_\theta,\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\right\}.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear algebraic propagation engine
nodes.notes: Apply `AE-21` with $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. For $\eta\ge1$, the stated trigger may be vacuous after constants are fixed. The endpoint remains blocked; no claim of verified progress is inferred from its presentation.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$, there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every accepted-incidence instance of density $\epsilon$, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Primitive factor allocation
nodes.notes: This starts the retained factorwise fallback. Researcher-0005 and researcher-0007 have enclosing verdict `revise`; they remain planning evidence only.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Factor the primitive squarefree relation as $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i.$$ Every $C_i$ is irreducible and $Z$-dependent, and $$s\le\deg_ZB\le\frac{\Delta}{d}\le\frac Dd\le K_\theta.$$ The lines in $T\setminus T_H$ admit a disjoint allocation $$T\setminus T_H=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^sT_i$$ such that $$C_i(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0
\qquad(L\in T_i).$$

nodes.label: Assigned-factor polar budget
nodes.notes: The cited factorwise calculations have exact line audits but enclosing verdict `revise`. This branch is unnecessary on the primary bounded-weight route but remains useful if whole-relation cleanup or template compression must be replaced.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Put $$\delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}C_i,
\qquad r_i=\deg_ZC_i,
\qquad \gamma_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_{i,Z}),$$ and $$\Xi_i=(r_i-1)\delta_i+r_i\gamma_i-dr_i(r_i-1).$$ If $b_i$ is the number of lines in $T_i$ on which $C_{i,Z}(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0$, then $$b_i\le\min\{|T_i|,\Xi_i\},
\qquad \gamma_i\le\delta_i-d,
\qquad \Xi_i\le\frac{\delta_i^2}{d}-\delta_i.$$ Every other line in $T_i$ contains at most $\gamma_i$ accepted points $x$ satisfying $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))=0$.

nodes.label: Normalized factorwise ramification cleanup
nodes.notes: This is the fallback assigned-factor deletion, charged directly to total normalized mass. Its sources have enclosing verdict `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Delete all edges on content lines, all edges assigned to identically ramified factor lines, and every remaining assigned edge $(x,L)$ for which $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))=0$. The surviving set $E_{\mathrm{cl}}$ satisfies $$\mu(E\setminus E_{\mathrm{cl}})\le\frac{D^2/d-D}{p(p+1)}+\frac{D-d}{p},
\qquad \mu(E_{\mathrm{cl}})\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2}.$$ Every surviving edge assigned to $i$ satisfies $$C_i(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Heavy clean factor and simple seed
nodes.notes: This is an elementary averaging step using only total edge mass. The strict seed inequality follows from the parameter slack in `AE-13`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Partition $$E_{\mathrm{cl}}= igsqcup_{i=1}^sE_i,
\qquad 
u_i=\mu(E_i).$$ Some $i$ satisfies $$
u_i\ge rac{a_	heta\epsilon}{2K_	heta}$$ and has a point $b$ incident in $E_i$ to more than $\delta_i$ distinct lines, with $$C_i(b,f(b))=0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(b,f(b))
e0.$$

nodes.label: Simple-pencil factor linearization
nodes.notes: Formal implicit uniqueness uses only the nonzero scalar $C_Z(b,\alpha)$. The cited sources have enclosing verdict `revise`, and no accept-audited source states this exact standalone factor package. The hypothesis is indispensable by `AE-11`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible and $Z$-dependent with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}C\le D<p$. Suppose $$C(b,\alpha)=0,
\qquad C_Z(b,\alpha)\ne0,$$ and more than $\Delta$ distinct lines $L_v(t)=b+tv$ carry $P_v\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ satisfying $$\deg P_v\le d,
\qquad P_v(0)=\alpha,
\qquad C(b+tv,P_v(t))=0.$$ Then there are a total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ and $u\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ such that $$C=u(Z-Q).$$

nodes.label: Disconnected factor aggregation
nodes.notes: The irreducible factor is global, so disconnected clean pieces assigned to it charge the same polynomial. The cited GENIUS aggregation step is unaudited.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $C_i=u(Z-Q)$ be supplied by `AE-19`, and let $X_i$ be the point endpoints of $E_i$. Then $$Q(x)=f(x)
\qquad(x\in X_i)$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{|X_i|}{p^2}\ge\nu_i\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2K_\theta}.$$

nodes.label: Uniform-jet rank barrier
nodes.notes: The source is audit-inexact with verdict `revise`. This is a diagnostic for raw uniform multiplicity counting, not an input to the primary route.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For positive integers $s,D,n,h$ with $d\le D<p$ and $n>D$, put $$C_s(D,d)=\sum_{a+b<s}\max\{D-a-db+1,0\}.$$ If $$\dim V_D>nC_s(D,d),
\qquad sh>D,$$ then $$h^2>\frac{dn}{12}.$$

nodes.label: Singular-seed guardrail
nodes.notes: All cited steps have exact accept audits. This rules out any propagation lemma based only on irreducibility and many compatible directions.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For admissible choices with $d+1<p$, there is a primitive, squarefree, absolutely irreducible polynomial $$C=XZ+H(Y),
\qquad \operatorname{wdeg}C=d+1,$$ supporting more than $d+1$ compatible degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines through one common lift, while no total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ satisfies $$C(X,Y,Q)=0.$$ At the common lift, $C_Z=0$.

nodes.label: Graph-only reaching obstruction
nodes.notes: Researcher-0002 supplies exact accept evidence. Researcher-0009 gives a stronger connected full-support and fractional-cover version, but its enclosing verdict is `revise`. These are method barriers, not counterexamples to the target.
nodes.statement_markdown: For suitable admissible constant-label instances with $$\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K,$$ every line family $R$ for which at least half of the accepted points of every accepted line are also incident to a distinct line of $R$ satisfies $$|R|\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ although a constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: High-popularity-tail decoder
nodes.notes: The enclosing audit verdict is `revise`. This records the usable high-tail corollary of the asymmetric decoder and leaves the complementary low-tail case to `AE-12`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For each point $x$, let $$a_x=|\{L:(x,L)\in\mathcal I\}|,
\qquad \delta_j=p^{-2}|\{x:a_x\ge j\}|,
\qquad u_*=\max_{1\le j\le p+1}j\delta_j.$$ If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{\epsilon}{12800}.$$

summary: Round 4 replaces the primary heavy-factor/simple-pencil branch by a shorter whole-relation component-template chain. Rank deficiency yields a squarefree relation, reached roots extend it to all carrier lines, coefficient-content removal makes the relation primitive, and the characteristic-safe raw resultant bounds ramified lines and derivative-zero edges. A new one-sided pruning step deletes only cleaned point vertices of degree at most $D$, retaining $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ mass while giving every component a simple seed with more than $D$ directions. Formal implicit lifting produces one degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial per component; every such template contributes a divisor $Z-Q$ of the common relation, so at most $D/d\le K_\theta$ templates occur and one captures $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ global agreement. The factorwise route is retained as a fallback. The bounded-weight label-aware dichotomy `AE-12` remains open, and the generalized cleanup, component lift, and compression packages still lack standalone accept audits.
target_statement: Prove an algebraic interpolation-and-propagation lemma strong enough to preserve a near-linear power of the accepted incidence density over $\mathbb F_p^2$.
title: Algebraic propagation engine
